Industrial Next and BMW will evaluate flexible robotic manipulation

Simulation and demonstrations train reconfigurable workstations; rapid changeovers remain company claims.

TechCrunch ↗13 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3Videos 1

A manufacturing evaluation

At TechCrunch Disrupt, Industrial Next announced a partnership with BMW Group Technology Office to evaluate AI-driven dexterous manipulation. Its self-contained robotic stations use proprietary models connecting vision, task context and motion.

Learning through simulation

Detailed physics simulation and demonstrations teach tasks instead of fixed scripts. Stations can be reconfigured and redeployed. The founders report smartphone applications including flex-cable handling and film peeling, but do not identify that customer.

BMW results are still outstanding

The company claims changeovers in minutes rather than weeks. The article provides no BMW measurements or independent validation. The partnership is an evaluation, not confirmation of a factory-wide rollout or fully autonomous end-to-end car production.
